title: Suite run blind again: the routine's prod CLI session expired after 8 unread warnings
service: echopoint-investigation routine (prod-org flow suites on dev)
summary: The 18:08Z run of the scheduled flow-suite routine checked no flow: `run_suites.sh` stopped with `AUTH-EXPIRED`. The `prod` CLI profile still held only a 7-day browser session (signed in about 2026-10-29T17:09Z), which expired at 2026-11-05T17:09:37Z. This is a regression of the [2026-10-26 postmortem](2026-10-26-suite-cli-session-expired.md): its preflight worked and warned in 8 runs, and the CLI fallback (echopoint-cli#81) merged on 2026-11-02, but the one action that removes the trigger, storing a CI-org API key, had no date or owner who saw it, and the warnings only reached run reports. The ledger row was marked verified on two clean runs while that action was still open. Gates passed on the two backend merges of the window (echopoint 53/53, anchor 32/32), so no change went unchecked.

impact.text: One routine run (of four a day) checked 0 of 85 flows, and every later run stays blind until a human signs in or stores a key. New coverage for echopoint#746 and #747 waits. Customers saw nothing: the flows only target dev, and gates and the Daily monitor use separate credentials.

trigger: The `prod` profile's session JWT reached its `exp` at 2026-11-05T17:09:37Z.
detection: The 18:08Z run's preflight stopped with `AUTH-EXPIRED` before any launch, as designed. The expiry itself was predicted: `AUTH-EXPIRES-SOON` appeared in 8 run logs from 2026-11-03T18:08Z and in the Run notes as an urgent open item, but no notification reached a human.
resolution: Not resolved by the routine: re-authentication needs a person, and the routine never enters credentials. The routine now pushes a notification for every `AUTH-EXPIRES-SOON` or `AUTH-EXPIRED` line, and a ledger row whose trigger depends on an open human action can no longer be marked verified.

whys.problem: The 18:08Z routine run checked no flow, so a dev regression merged now goes unseen until a human acts

because.text: The prod CLI profile's browser session expired at 17:09Z and the preflight stopped the run
The host still held only a 7-day browser session; the 2026-10-26 action A1 (store a CI-org API key) never happened
The first fix renewed the session, which cleared the symptom for exactly 7 days, and the row was then marked verified
because.evidence: Ledger row status `verified (2026-10-30T17:08Z)` while A1 was open

because.text: The loop marks a row verified after two clean runs even when the trigger returns on a known date unless an open human action is done
A1 had a due date in a committed document but no channel that reminds its owner
Human actions from postmortems live only in docs and Run notes; nothing pushes them when their deadline nears
The expiry was predicted 48 h ahead in 8 runs, yet no human acted before it
The warning went only to the run log, the Run notes and the run's final report
The routine pushes a notification per postmortem only, so a dated warning that needs a human never reaches one
Recovery waits for a person: the routine cannot sign in and must not handle credentials
Browser sign-in is the only credential on the host, and it needs a person at a browser
Creating an org API key is an org-admin action outside the routine's scope
The routine host has no non-expiring credential, though echopoint-cli#81 now makes a stored API key work after a session expires

contributing: The Run notes held the expiry as open item 41 marked URGENT, but the Run notes are read only by the next run, not by the human who must act.
Post-deploy gates and the Daily monitor stayed green on separate credentials, so nothing else looked wrong.

well: The preflight caught the expiry before any launch: no half-run flows, no leaked cleanup.
Gates covered the window: both backend merges (echopoint#746, #747) passed 53/53 on dev before prod.
wrong: A predicted, dated failure happened anyway after 8 warnings.
The first postmortem's verified status hid that its prevent action was still open.
lucky: The two backend merges of the window were small security fixes that the CI gates covered.
The expiry hit between runs, not during one.

actions.what: Create a CI-org API key for the routine and store it: `echopoint auth login --profile prod --api-key <key> --default` (echopoint-cli#81 makes it survive the session); sign in again meanwhile
Routine pushes a notification for every `AUTH-EXPIRES-SOON` or `AUTH-EXPIRED` preflight line, and for any dated human action due within 48 h
`postmortem-loop.md` §5: a row whose trigger returns unless an open human action is done stays `fix-live`, never `verified`
flow-suite-testing skill: a renewed browser session is a mitigation, not a fix; the run stays at risk until an API key is stored

messaging.internal: Flow suites are blind since 17:09Z: the routine's prod CLI session expired again. Please store a CI-org API key with `echopoint auth login --profile prod --api-key <key> --default` (or sign in again). Gates and Daily are unaffected.
